name: Raw mean difference (independent groups)
variables: Ybar1 = sample mean of group 1 (treatment); Ybar2 = sample mean of group 2 (control/placebo); delta_hat = estimate of the population mean difference delta = mu1 - mu2.
notes: Worked: Ex 8.1 Ginkgo 58.4 - placebo 56.8 = 1.6. effect_sizes.md returns the MD with the unequal-variance variance S1²/n1 + S2²/n2.

name: Pooled within-group variance
variables: n1, n2 = group sample sizes; S1, S2 = group sample SDs; Sp^2 = pooled variance (equal population variances assumed).
notes: Worked: Ex 8.1 Sp² = 16.303. effect_sizes.pooled_sd returns Sp (the square root). The same pooled SD s* is the denominator of the book's 'Hedges g' and of MetaXL 'Cohen'.

name: Variance of the raw MD assuming equal variances
variables: n1, n2 = group sample sizes; Sp^2 = pooled within-group variance; V_eq, SE_eq = variance and standard error of Ybar1 - Ybar2.
notes: Worked: Ex 8.1 V_eq = 1.261542, SE_eq = 1.1232. The engine's effect_sizes.md uses only the unequal-variance form.

name: Variance of the raw MD with unequal variances
variables: S1, S2 = group sample SDs; n1, n2 = group sample sizes.
notes: Worked: Ex 8.1 V_neq = 1.286131, SE_neq = 1.1341. The book defers unequal-variance issues to Ch 9 (MD).

name: Matched-pairs mean difference and its variance
expression: D_i = Y1i - Y2i ;  Dbar = sum(D_i)/n ;  S_D^2 = sum((D_i - Dbar)^2)/(n - 1) ;  Var(Dbar) = S_D^2/n ;  SE(Dbar) = sqrt(S_D^2/n)
variables: Y1i, Y2i = paired observations for pair i (e.g. baseline and follow-up); n = number of pairs; D_i = within-pair difference; Dbar = mean difference; S_D^2 = sample variance of the differences.
notes: Worked: Ex 8.2 n = 15, sum D = 254, sum (D - Dbar)² = 2808.9333 → Dbar = 16.9333, S_D² = 200.6381, Var = 13.3759, SE = 3.6573. In the example D = baseline - 6-week value, so positive = reduction. No paired SMD (d_z, d_av) is given in the chapter.

name: Population standardized mean difference
variables: mu1, mu2 = population means of treatment and control; sigma = common population SD (sigma1 = sigma2 = sigma assumed).
notes: Definition only; d, g and Δ differ in how sigma is estimated.

name: Cohen's d as printed in the book (n-denominator pooled SD)
expression: d = (Xbar1 - Xbar2) / s ;  s = sqrt[ (n1*S1^2 + n2*S2^2) / (n1 + n2) ]
variables: Xbar1, Xbar2 = group means; S1, S2 = group SDs; n1, n2 = group sizes; s = n-denominator pooled SD (called a biased estimator of sigma).
notes: [R] Fragments read 'n1 S2 + n2 S2 … n1 + n2'. MetaXL/admetan 'Cohen' does NOT use this SD: it uses the (n-1) pooled SD (see F-KHN08-008). Using this d with the printed Var(d) gives Q = 163.29 for the operative-time data, which does not match the printed 163.89. The engine has no n-denominator SMD.

name: SMD with (n-1) pooled SD (book's 'Hedges g' without J; MetaXL 'Cohen')
variables: Xbar1, Xbar2 = group means; S1, S2 = group SDs; n1, n2 = group sizes; s* = (n-1) pooled SD.
notes: The book's text calls this Hedges' g but applies no small-sample correction; MetaXL/admetan call it 'Cohen'. Engine: effect_sizes.smd(..., correct=False) (measure COHEN_D) gives this point estimate, but its default variance (vtype='LS', 2N denominator) differs from the 2(N-2) form used by MetaXL 'Cohen'.

name: Small-sample correction factor J (approximation)
variables: N = n1 + n2; df = N - 2; g = SMD with (n-1) pooled SD; g* = bias-corrected ('unbiased') SMD.
notes: Not printed in the chapter; inferred from Table 8.2 (N = 76: J = 0.98983, 0.72 → 0.71) and from MetaXL 'Hedges' output. Engine: effect_sizes.hedges_j(N - 2, method='approx'); the engine default is the exact gamma-function J. effect_sizes.smd(..., correct=True, j_method='approx') gives the MetaXL 'Hedges' point estimate.

name: Glass's delta
variables: Xbar1, Xbar2 = treatment and control means; s2 = SD of the control group only.
notes: Glass, McGaw & Smith 1981. MetaXL 'Glass' uses the same definition. In Ex 8.12 it moves Bonjer from 1.58 to 1.89. Not implemented in the engine.

name: Variance of Cohen's d as printed
variables: n1, n2 = group sizes; d = Cohen's d (book definition); population version uses theta in place of d.
notes: [R] Fragments: 'n1+n2 … n1 n2 … 2(n1+n2-2) × n1+n2 / n1+n2-2'. Software (MetaXL 'Cohen') does not use this inflated form; it uses N/(n1 n2) + d²/(2(N-2)) with the (n-1) pooled-SD d.

name: Variance of the SMD with 2(N-2) denominator (book's Var(g); MetaXL 'Cohen')
variables: n1, n2 = group sizes; g = SMD with (n-1) pooled SD (MetaXL 'Cohen' d); N = n1 + n2.
notes: [R] Worked: Ex 8.3 g = 0.72, N = 76 (assumed 38/38) → Var = 0.056134, SE = 0.236927; reproduces only with 2(N-2) = 148. Same formula reproduces MetaXL 'Cohen' (Q = 163.885 for the operative-time data). Not in the engine (effect_sizes.smd offers LS = 2N, LS2, UB).

name: Variance of Glass's delta
variables: n1, n2 = treatment and control group sizes; Delta = Glass's delta.
notes: The SE paragraph on p. 166 prints '2(n2 - 2)', a typo; MetaXL 'Glass' output (Q = 179.401) matches n2 - 1. Not implemented in the engine.

name: SMD variance with 2N denominator (Hedges 1985 open-education data)
expression: Var(theta_hat) = (nE + nC)/(nE*nC) + theta_hat^2 / (2*(nE + nC)) ;  with nE = nC = n: Var = 2/n + theta_hat^2/(4n)
variables: nE, nC = experimental and control group sizes; theta_hat = study SMD; n = common arm size.
notes: [R] Worked: Study 1 n = 22, theta = 0.563 → Var = 0.094511, SE = 0.307426. This equals the engine's effect_sizes.smd vtype='LS' form (1/n1 + 1/n2 + y²/(2N)) and metafor's escalc('SMD') large-sample variance. Inconsistent with the 2(N-2) form used elsewhere in the chapter.

name: MetaXL/admetan 'Hedges' g and its variance
variables: d = SMD with (n-1) pooled SD; N = n1 + n2; n1, n2 = group sizes; J = approximate small-sample correction.
notes: Reverse-engineered by the note-taker (not printed in the book); agrees with Stata metan/admetan documentation. Reproduces Q = 163.590, Bonjer FE weight 26.0%, Ng 2008 CI (0.68, 1.53); 2(N-2) instead gives Q = 163.65. The engine does not implement the 2(N-3.94) variance; R metafor gives Q = 163.71.

name: Wald confidence interval for a study or pooled SMD
variables: theta_hat = study or pooled estimate; SE = its standard error; z_{alpha/2} = upper alpha/2 standard normal quantile.
notes: Worked: g = 0.72, SE = 0.236927 → (0.256, 1.184). No transformation is needed for the SMD (unlike OR/RR). Used for every model in the chapter (FE, RE, IVhet).

name: z-test for an SMD (study or pooled)
expression: Z = theta_hat / SE(theta_hat) ~ N(0,1) under H0: theta = 0 ;  P = 2 * P(Z > |z0|) ;  reject if |z0| >= z_{alpha/2} or P <= alpha
variables: theta_hat = estimate; SE = standard error; z0 = observed Z; alpha = significance level.

name: Fixed-effect (inverse-variance) pooled estimate
expression: w_i = 1/v_i ;  theta_FE = sum(w_i*theta_i)/sum(w_i) ;  Var(theta_FE) = 1/sum(w_i) ;  SE = sqrt(1/sum(w_i))
variables: theta_i = study SMD; v_i = its variance; w_i = inverse-variance weight; k = number of studies.
notes: Worked: Open Education sum w = 69.55727, sum w*theta = 1.478124 → theta_FE = 0.02125, Var = 0.014377, SE = 0.119903, CI (-0.21, 0.26). Engine: models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='fixed', ci_method='z'). MetaXL model 'IV'. [note: the book's rule of using FE when heterogeneity is 'insignificant' is outdated; choose the model a priori (Cochrane v6).]

name: Percentage (normalised) study weights
expression: weight%_i = 100 * w_i / sum_j(w_j)  (FE and IVhet: w_i = 1/v_i ; RE: w_i* = 1/(v_i + tau2_hat), w_i** = w_i*/sum_j w_j*)
variables: w_i = FE inverse-variance weight; w_i* = RE weight; w_i** = normalised RE weight (sums to 1); tau2_hat = DL between-study variance.
notes: The book says the w* add up to 1; only the normalised w** do. IVhet % weights equal FE % weights. Engine returns them as weights_pct in models.meta_analysis.

name: DerSimonian–Laird between-study variance
expression: tau2_hat = (Q - df)/C ;  C = sum(w_i) - sum(w_i^2)/sum(w_i) ;  df = k - 1
variables: Q = Cochran's Q with FE weights; w_i = 1/v_i; k = number of studies; C = scaling constant.
notes: Worked: Open Education Q = 7.5104, C = 52.62122 → tau2 = 0.047707. Truncation at 0 when Q < df is not stated in the book; the engine truncates (max(0, ·)). Ex 8.10 swaps the two Q terms in its formula line. Cochrane Handbook v6 prefers REML/PM (engine: models.tau2_reml, models.tau2_pm).

name: Random-effects (DL) pooled estimate
expression: w_i* = 1/(v_i + tau2_hat) ;  theta_RE = sum(w_i*·theta_i)/sum(w_i*) ;  SE = sqrt(1/sum(w_i*)) ;  CI = theta_RE ± 1.96*SE
variables: v_i = within-study variance; tau2_hat = DL estimate; w_i* = RE weight; theta_i = study SMD.
notes: Worked: Open Education sum w* = 40.4085, sum w*theta = 3.39399 → theta_RE = 0.083967, SE = 0.157313, CI (-0.2244, 0.3923). Engine: models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='random', tau2_method='DL', ci_method='z') to reproduce the book (engine defaults are REML + HKSJ). MetaXL model 'RE'.

name: IVhet variance (Doi et al. 2015a)
expression: theta_IVhet = sum(w_i*theta_i)/sum(w_i), w_i = 1/v_i ;  Var(theta_IVhet) = sum_i [ (w_i/sum_j w_j)^2 * (v_i + tau2_hat) ] ;  SE = sqrt(Var)
variables: w_i = FE inverse-variance weight; v_i = within-study variance; tau2_hat = DL between-study variance; theta_i = study SMD.
notes: [R] Printed fragments are garbled; verified numerically. Study 1 term: (10.581/69.557)² × 0.14222 = 0.00329. Worked: theta = 0.021251, sum W* = 0.02599, SE = 0.16122, CI (-0.294744, 0.33725). Ex 8.11's CI line wrongly plugs in 0.083967. Call via models.meta_analysis(model='ivhet'). [note: IVhet is the Doi group's model (Khan co-authored Doi 2015a); it is not in Cochrane Handbook v6, which uses RE (REML/PM, optionally HKSJ) plus a prediction interval.]

name: Cochran's Q
expression: Q = sum(w_i*(theta_i - theta_FE)^2) = sum(((theta_i - theta_FE)/s_i)^2) = sum(w_i*theta_i^2) - (sum(w_i*theta_i))^2/sum(w_i)
variables: w_i = 1/v_i (FE weights); s_i = sqrt(v_i); theta_FE = FE pooled estimate; theta_i = study SMD.
notes: Worked: Open Education Q = 7.541822 - 1.478124²/69.55727 = 7.51041. Ex 8.9 omits the square in the text formula line. Operative time: Q = 163.89 (d), 163.59 (g), 179.40 (Δ). Always computed with FE weights, so identical across FE/RE/IVhet outputs. E(Q) = df under H0; Q - df = excess variation.

name: Q test of homogeneity
expression: H0: theta_1 = ... = theta_k ;  Q ~ chi2_{k-1} ;  P = P(chi2_{k-1} >= Q) ;  reject if Q >= chi2_{k-1,1-alpha} or P <= alpha
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; k = number of studies; alpha = significance level.
notes: Worked: Q = 7.51, df = 5, P = 0.19; chi2_5 10% critical value 9.236. Ex 8.9 writes P(chi2_5 >= 7.536) for 7.51. Low power: a non-significant P does not prove homogeneity. models.heterogeneity returns p_Q.

name: I² statistic
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; df = k - 1.
notes: Worked: Q = 7.51041, df = 5 → I² = 0.334257 → 33%; operative time 95%, 95%, 96%. Truncation at 0 not stated in the book; the engine uses max(0, ·). No thresholds given in the chapter. [note: Cochrane v6 gives overlapping bands (0–40%, 30–60%, 50–90%, 75–100%) that are not absolute rules; report τ² and a prediction interval as well.]

name: Doi plot Z-score (Furuya-Kanamori algorithm)
expression: sort studies by theta_i ;  N_i = 100*max(v)/v_i ;  MR_1 = N_1/2, MR_i = MR_{i-1} + (N_{i-1} + N_i)/2 ;  p_i = (MR_i - 0.5)/sum(N) ;  Z_i = Phi^{-1}(p_i) ;  plot |Z_i| vs theta_i ;  apex m = argmin |Z_i|
variables: theta_i = study effect size; v_i = its variance; N_i = rescaled inverse-variance weight; MR_i = cumulative mid-rank; p_i = percentile; Phi^{-1} = standard normal quantile function; |Z_i| = ordinate of the Doi plot; m = apex study.
notes: [R] Not given in the chapter (it cites Doi 2018 and Furuya-Kanamori et al. 2018). The engine's bias.doi_plot_data (metasens::lfkindex algorithm) reproduces the plotted points for Cohen's d with the MetaXL variances: |Z| = 1.38 (Stevenson), 0.83 (Lujan), 0.47 (Fleshman), 0.18 (Zhou), 0.04 (Jeong, apex), 0.33 (Liang), 0.53 (Ng 2008), 0.61 (Ng 2014), 1.13 (Bonjer). The simpler p_i = (sum_{j<i} w_j + w_i/2)/sum(w) differs only by 0.5/sum(N) and gives the same values to 2 decimals. [note: a Doi-group method, not part of Cochrane Handbook v6 guidance.]

name: LFK index (Doi plot asymmetry)
expression: d_i = theta_i - theta_m ;  LFK = 5/(2k) * sum_i [ Z_i + (max Z - min Z)/(max d - min d) * d_i ] ;  |LFK| <= 1 no asymmetry, 1 < |LFK| <= 2 minor, |LFK| > 2 major
variables: theta_i, Z_i = sorted effect sizes and signed Doi-plot Z-scores (F-KHN08-026); theta_m = effect size of the apex study (smallest |Z|); k = number of studies.
notes: [R] The formula is not printed in Ch 8; it is the Furuya-Kanamori et al. (2018) algorithm as implemented in metasens::lfkindex and in the engine. With the MetaXL variances it reproduces the printed values: 0.531 → 0.53 for Cohen's d (Fig. 8.8) and 0.522 → 0.52 for Hedges' g (Fig. 8.10), both 'No asymmetry'. [note: the thresholds are the developers' heuristics, and the LFK index is not part of Cochrane Handbook v6 guidance; Glass's Δ on the same data gives 1.73 (minor asymmetry).]
